title: An opioid efficacy switch for reversible optical control of analgesia
title_zh: 可逆光控阿片类镇痛的阿片受体效能切换
abstract: The mu-opioid receptor (MOR) is a major target for pain treatment, but its effectiveness is limited by dangerous side effects. However, the systemic administration of opioids makes it difficult both to decipher their underlying mechanisms of action and to limit drug action to specific receptor subpopulations to isolate therapeutic effects from adverse effects. Here, we develop a reversibly photoswitchable morphinan agonist termed "azo-morphine-3" (AM-3) that interconverts from low to high efficacy in response to light to enable optical control of MOR signaling. Structural analysis of the low ("trans") and high ("cis") efficacy states of AM-3 bound to the MOR reveals distinct binding modes, with each state driving unique ligand, receptor, and G protein dynamics. In mice, AM-3 drives reversible and repeatable optical control of antinociception across pain models with a reduced side effect profile owing to its limited brain accumulation and its ability to be locally activated.
abstract_zh: μ-阿片受体（MOR）是疼痛治疗的主要靶点，但其疗效受危险副作用限制。系统给药使得难以阐明阿片的作用机制，并难以将药物作用限定于特定受体亚群，以分离治疗效应与不良反应。我们开发了一种可逆光开关的莫尔啡胺激动剂，称为 "azo-morphine-3"（AM-3），其在光照下可在低效能（trans）与高效能（cis）之间互变，从而实现对MOR信号的光学控制。对AM-3与MOR结合的低效能和高效能状态进行结构分析，发现两种状态具有不同的结合模式，每种状态驱动独特的配体、受体和G蛋白动力学。在小鼠中，AM-3实现了可逆且可重复的光学控制抗痛感，且由于其在脑内积累有限且可局部激活，副作用谱显著降低。
